problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
r=⟨{t}^{2}{e}^{-2t},\,(t-1)^{3}⟩,\,t\in [0,\infty ).
$$

Calculate the times at which the particle is stationary.

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Times at Which a Particle Is Stationary
examples.problem:
A particle $P$ moves in the $x$-$y$ plane (relative to a fixed origin $O$) with position vector

$$
\mathbf{r} = \langle t^2-2t, t^3-3t \rangle, \quad t\in[0,\infty).
$$

Calculate the times at which the particle is stationary.
examples.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $\mathbf{v}.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-3t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t-2,\,3{t}^{2}-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The particle is stationary when its velocity is zero. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =0 \\ ⟨2t-2,3{t}^{2}-3⟩ & =⟨0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So we need

$$
\begin{aligned}2t-2 & =0\,⇒\,t=1, \\ 3{t}^{2}-3 & =0\,⇒\,t=\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $t=-1$ is outside of the domain of $t,$ so we discard it. 

The solution $t=1$ is the only solution that satisfies both equations, so this is the only time when the object is stationary.

feedback.problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{{4}^{t-1}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4},\frac{{9}^{t-1}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡9}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle at time $t=1.$

The speed at time $t=1$ is
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity vector $v.$ Differentiating the position vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{4}^{t-1}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{9}^{t-1}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡9})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{{4}^{t-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡4},\frac{{9}^{t-1}\operatorname{ln}⁡9}{\operatorname{ln}⁡9}⟩ \\  & =⟨{4}^{t-1},{9}^{t-1}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=1,$ we substitute in the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨{4}^{1-1},{9}^{1-1}⟩=⟨1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed at $t=1$ we calculate the magnitude of $v(1),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|v(1)| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
